core_obligations: Handle the easy case (proof lines 850-856): let T_0 be the set of points of T which do not specialize nontrivially to another point of T; if T_0 is infinite then it is the required subset, so assume T_0 finite.

Build the strata (proof lines 856-878): define T_i inductively as the set of points outside the earlier strata which specialize nontrivially to a point of T_{i-1} and whose every nontrivial specialization into T lands in the earlier strata; if any T_i is infinite it is the required subset.

Show the strata exhaust (proof lines 878-892): with d the maximum of the dimensions of the local rings at the points of the finite set T_0, a chain of i nontrivial specializations ending in T_0 consists of points of the spectrum of the local ring at its endpoint, so i is at most d and all strata beyond d are empty; hence the union of the strata is finite.

Conclude (proof lines 892-906): a point of T outside the finite union must specialize nontrivially to another such point, since otherwise maximality of the index would put it into a later stratum; iterating produces an infinite chain of nontrivial specializations among points of T outside the union, which is impossible because the underlying space is Noetherian.
proof_roadmap: Collect the points with no nontrivial specialization into T and assume that collection finite.
Define the strata of points whose specializations into T lie in earlier strata and show they run out after finitely many steps.
Show that the complement of the finite union would produce an infinite descending chain, contradicting Noetherianness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that every infinite subset T of a Noetherian scheme contains an infinite subset T' whose points admit no nontrivial specializations among themselves (statement lines 843-848). The proof (proof lines 850-893) separates off the points with no nontrivial specialization into T, defines finitely many strata whose specializations into T stay in earlier strata, shows the strata exhaust the subset, and rules out the complement by producing an infinite chain of specializations contradicting Noetherianness. H3: an original stratification argument with a dimension bound and a Noetherianity contradiction, written out in full.
